titulo_it: Avere o essere en passato prossimo

texto: The vast majority of transient verbs (those that admit direct object: mangiare, leggere, comprare, fare, ascoltare) and many activity intransitions (parlare, telephone, camminare, lavorare) use **avere**. The faulty participle ends neuter in **-o**: **Ho telefonato a mia madre**.

The verbs of oriented movement (andare, venire, partire, arrivare, tornare, uscire, entrare), state change (nancere, morire, divenwill), permanence (stare, rimanere) and reflexive use **essere** with mandatory agreement: **Sono arrivata a Roma**.

bloques.titulo: Vocabulary: choice of assistant and daily life

frases.it: Giulia, ho telefonato a casa tua sabato pomeriggio, ma non hai risposto!
frases.es: ¡Giulia, llamé a tu casa el sábado por la tarde, pero no respondiste!
frases.en: Giulia, I called your house Saturday afternoon, but you didn't answer!

frases.it: Mi dispiace, Marco! Sono uscita presto e sono andata in centro.
frases.es: ¡Lo siento, Marco! Salí temprano y fui al centro.
frases.en: I'm sorry, Marco! I got out early and went downtown.

frases.it: E che cosa hai fatto in centro?
frases.en: And what did you do in the middle?

frases.it: Ho incontrato Sara e siamo andate insieme al museo.
frases.es: Me encontré con Sara y fuimos juntas al museo.
frases.en: I met Sara and we went to the museum together.

frases.it: Che cosa avete visto al museo?
frases.en: What did you see at the museum?

frases.it: Abbiamo guardato una bella mostra. Poi abbiamo cenato in pizzeria.
frases.es: Vimos una hermosa exposición. Luego cenamos en una pizzería.
frases.en: We saw a beautiful exhibition. Then we had dinner at a pizzeria.

frases.it: E a che ora sei tornata a casa?
frases.es: ¿Y a qué hora volviste a casa?
frases.en: And what time did you come home?

frases.it: Sono tornata a mezzanotte, molto stanca ma contenta!
frases.es: ¡Volví a medianoche, muy cansada pero contenta!
frases.en: I came back at midnight, very tired but happy!

bloques.pregunta: What auxiliary does the «telefonare» verb require in prossimo passage?

opciones.explicacion: «Telefonare» is a verb of communicative action that always governs «avere».
«Telefonare» does not involve displacement or change of status.
«Stare» is not used as an auxiliary in composite times.

bloques.pregunta: How does Giulia (woman) say she has arrived in Rome?

opciones.explicacion: The verb «arrivare» governs «essere» and the participle matches feminine (-a).
The -or denotes masculine singular subject termination.

bloques.pregunta: Complete with the correct form of «andare».
bloques.frase: Ieri sera Sara e Giulia sono ___ insieme in centro.

opciones.explicacion: feminine plural subject with «essere» auxiliary: the mandatory desinence is -e.
The deinence -i is for men or mixed groups.
It is singular form of feminine, not plural.

bloques.frase: Ho telefonato a mia madre ieri sera.

opciones.texto: I phoned my mother last night.
opciones.explicacion: «Ho telefonato» is the prossimo passage of the phone with a break.

opciones.texto: My mother called me last night.
opciones.explicacion: The subject is «io» (ho phone), not the mother.

opciones.texto: I'm gonna call my mother on the phone today.
opciones.explicacion: The phrase expresses an action already completed in the past.

bloques.frase: Sara e Giulia sono uscite insieme alle otto.

opciones.texto: Sara and Giulia went out together at 8: 00.
Sara and Giulia ate together at 8: 00.
opciones.explicacion: The verb is to use (come out), not mangiare (eat).

opciones.texto: Sara and Giulia called together at 8: 00.

bloques.frase: Abbiamo guardato una bella mostra al museo
bloques.traduccion: We've seen a beautiful exhibition at the museum.
bloques.explicacion: Subject to us with regular variable averse and participle.

bloques.pregunta: Why do you say «ho incontrato Sara» but «sono andata con Sara»?

opciones.explicacion: The choice of the auxiliary depends on the syntactic properties of each verb.

opciones.texto: Porque «Sara» es un nombre femenino singular.
opciones.explicacion: The direct object does not determine the choice between fault and essere.

opciones.texto: Because the two prayers are present as an indication.

intro: To master the Italian past you must know which verbs select «avere» and which ones choose «essere».
